text:
Macklin Celebrini played a career-high 28.1 minutes in Dallas on Saturday, and that number tells you where the Sharks are. They've lost seven of their last eight, Alexander Wennberg (back tonight) missed 10 games, and the 20-year-old captain has been asked to do almost everything. Asked by Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest about those minutes, coach Ryan Warsofsky said "it’s not ideal."

The production is down from last season's 115 points: 21 in 17 games, and 10 in his last 10 when our numbers expected about 14 at his ice time. Some of that is finishing. He's shooting 9.9%, below his usual range, with 7 goals on 8.1 expected. The process is fine: his own chances are worth 1.24 expected goals per 60 minutes, more than last season, and San Jose's share of expected goals is about 11 points better with him on the ice than without him.

What we'd watch now is whether Wennberg's return frees him up. Our range still has him around 111 points over the full season (95 to 128). Heavy minutes on a losing team wear on anyone; so far he's handling them better than the scoresheet says.
headline: Celebrini is carrying the Sharks, 28 minutes at a time
